title: assert() aborts on small/repeat-free inputs (asserts are live: no -DNDEBUG); related to the over-read in #257
body:
## Summary

Several estimators abort the whole program via `assert()` on small or repeat-free inputs, reachable from a file alone with the default command line. The shipped Makefile does not define `NDEBUG`, so these asserts are live in the `-O2` build; a user gets `Aborted` with no JSON and no estimate. This is the controlled-crash sibling of the heap over-read in #257 (same root cause: no minimum-length validation before the predictor/LRS estimators). Filed separately because this one is a clean abort, not a memory-safety violation.

## Reproductions

Built at `87c104d` (stock Makefile flags, asserts enabled):

```
printf '\x00\x01' > f2.bin          ; ./ea_non_iid f2.bin
#   Assertion failed: ((v>0) && (v < n)), function SAalgs32, file lrs_test.h, line 149

python3 -c "open('f3.bin','wb').write(bytes([0,1,0]))" ; ./ea_non_iid f3.bin
#   Assertion failed: (L>3), function binaryMultiMMCPredictionEstimate, multi_mmc_test.h:21

python3 -c "open('f17.bin','wb').write(bytes([i&1 for i in range(17)]))" ; ./ea_non_iid f17.bin
#   Assertion failed: (L-B_len > 2), function binaryLZ78YPredictionEstimate, lz78y_test.h:18
```

`L=2` (lrs_test.h:149), `L=3` (multi_mmc_test.h:21), and `L=17,18` (lz78y_test.h:18) all abort. `printf '\x00\x01'` (a 2-byte file) is enough. A repeat-free input also aborts SAalgs (all-distinct symbols give `v=0`).

## Impact

Denial of service / uninformative failure from an untrusted file. Where `NDEBUG` *is* defined (a hardened downstream build), the same tiny inputs instead reach the out-of-bounds accesses the asserts were masking (see #257).

## Suggested fix (not submitted as code)

Validate the input length once at intake and return a refusal (non-zero `errorLevel`, a message) rather than asserting deep inside each estimator; the same length guard closes #257.

Found during a memory-safety audit.
